Appearance:
 Shri Sankalp Kochar - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Amit Bhurrak - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State.
Shri S.K. Tiwari - Advocate for the objector.

Order 
This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.494/2024 registered at Police Station Nourazabad, District Umaria, for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n),
506 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 5(l)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The applicant is in jail since 23.03.2025.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the alleged offence.
It is submitted that the applicant is a government employee.

It is further submitted that though it is a case of prosecution that the applicant, on the false pretext of marriage, developed physical relations with the prosecutrix, but according to him, it is incorrect.

He has submitted that the applicant and prosecutrix were in affair for more than three years and during that period, physical relations got developed between them that too with the consent of the prosecutrix.

He has further submitted that looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, the contents of FIR and the material NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:17082 2 MCRC-14649-2025 available with the prosecution, it can be gathered that it was a case of consent and under the existing scenario, no offence under Section 376 of the IPC is made out against the applicant.

He has also submitted that the applicant was ready to get married with the prosecutrix,
Krishnapal Singh @ Suraj Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185887311/
1 but somehow, it could not be solemnized.

entities.text: Krishnapal Singh @ Suraj Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant may kindly be enlarged on bail.

3. On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer and learned counsel for the objector have opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that looking to the nature of crime committed by the applicant, he is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.
4. Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, on perusal of case diary and the fact that the applicant is an under trial accused, I am inclined to allow this application.
Thus, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this application is allowed.

5. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.
6. On being released, the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE dm Krishnapal Singh @ Suraj Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185887311/
